entities.name: Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party (ABLP), founded in 1946 by Vere Cornwall Bird — one of the Caribbean's most significant trade union and political leaders — has been the dominant political party in Antigua and Barbuda for most of the country's modern history, holding power for most of the years from 1956 to the present and guiding the twin-island nation through the transition from British colonial status to independence (1981) as one of the Caribbean's most continuous political dynasties, centered on the Bird family.

Vere Cornwall Bird's founding of the ABLP in the context of the Antiguan labor movement (after organizing the Antigua Trades and Labour Union) followed the pattern of Caribbean political development in which labor unions became the foundation of mass political movements that led to independence. This model — union organizing → political party → electoral politics → independence — was the typical trajectory of Caribbean decolonization, and Bird's ABLP was one of its most successful examples.

The Bird family's dominance of Antiguan politics — Vere Cornwall Bird served as premier/prime minister from 1960-1994, and his son Lester Bird served as prime minister from 1994-2004 — represents one of the Caribbean's most sustained political family dynasties. The ABLP's long rule has been associated with both Antigua's economic development (tourism-based economy, tax haven status) and controversy (Birdnest scandals, gun-running scandal involving Lester Bird's brother Vere Jr., and other corruption allegations).
